alloy.preparation: 30-kg ingots surface-ground, hot-rolled to 6 mm, annealed at 1100°C, cold-rolled to 2 mm, then annealed at 1050°C; punched discs. Polished to 600-grit SiC, degreased in 95% ethanol, air-dried, kept dry and dust-free for 24 h; dry-air stream before mounting.

test_solution.preparation: Deaerated with high-purity nitrogen; electrochemical vessels deaerated for 60 min before polarization.

test_method.procedure_description: EG&G disc holder with precautions against crevices. Initial potential −20 mV relative to Ecorr; scan toward a maximum 0.8 V (SCE), reverse at 0.5 × 10⁻³ A/cm², and return to Ecorr. Results showing crevice corrosion were rejected. Methods specify a 35°C water bath, conflicting with 30°C in Table 2.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Breakdown potential Eb from polarization; reverse-scan current threshold is 0.5 × 10⁻³ A/cm². Separate microscopy runs were stopped above 10⁻⁵ A/cm².

experiments.result_note: Table caption specifies 3.5% NaCl, 30°C; cyclic-polarization methods specify 3.5% NaCl, 35°C and figure captions 3% NaCl, 30°C. Retained as printed. Figures 17–18 summarize these base-metal results; overlapping symbols and inconsistent PREN positions are not used to relabel heats. Figure 18 repeats the base-metal comparison; near-PREN-24 readings overlap and remain approximate. Table 1 does not explicitly label a mass/atomic basis; composition amounts retain %. The printed F19-2Nb carbon entry is 0.0011; it is not silently changed to the different Table 4 heat composition.

Figure 8 is associated with 30°C in the registry; the supplied caption has an anomalous printed “300°C”, while the general methods say 35°C. This discrepancy is retained rather than interpreted as a new high-temperature test.

alloy.preparation: Industrial type 444 ferritic stainless steel considered theoretically.

test_method.procedure_description: Approximate theoretical breakdown potential from Equation (5), discussed for industrial type 444 stainless steel.

experiments.result_note: Authors’ approximate theoretical value according to Equation (5), compared qualitatively with cited literature; no separate cited numerical result is supplied. This theoretical example uses PREN 23–24.5 and approximately 300 oxide inclusions/mm², with sulfur <0.004%; no individual tested heat or separate test setup is specified.

alloy.preparation: 30-kg ingots surface-ground, hot-rolled to 6 mm, annealed at 1100°C, cold-rolled to 2 mm, then annealed at 1050°C; punched discs. Autogenous gas-tungsten arc bead-on-plate welding, 100 A at 60 cm/min (1.2 kJ/cm), argon purge and backing each 15 L/min. Fusion line centered in disc; polished to 600-grit SiC, degreased with 95% ethanol, dried and stored for 24 h.
alloy.microstructure: Ferritic stainless steel. Weld and heat-affected-zone regions; large columnar weld grains and coarsened HAZ grains described.

experiments.result_note: Graphical reading. Heat identities of clustered symbols are not individually printed; no alloy assignment inferred. These are welded results distinct from base-metal Table 2. General methods specify 3.5% NaCl at 35°C, whereas Table 2 gives 30°C and several figure captions give 3% NaCl. No unique temperature is resolved for this summary marker; its heat is not assigned from PREN alone.
experiments.failure_notes: Individual heat identity/composition cannot be recovered uniquely from the unlabeled/overlapping PREN markers in Figure 17.
